source.content:
Expected annual savings: $120,000 for 10 stores.
All-in annual cost: $40,000, including support.
Expected net benefit: $80,000 per year.
Proceed only after the inventory join (matching product records) passes a 2-week pilot.
If savings fall to $30,000, the annual net loss is $10,000.
Request pilot review
How the estimates work
$120,000 expected annual savings − $40,000 all-in annual cost = $80,000 expected annual net benefit.
10 stores × $12,000 expected savings per store per year = $120,000 expected savings per year.
Expected savings are a forecast, not measured results.
A sensitivity case checks how the decision changes when savings differ.
$30,000 downside annual savings − $40,000 all-in annual cost = a $10,000 annual net loss.

evidence: Authored full fixture source; model annotations, not independently qualified extraction

readerEvidence.audience: Business decision-makers unfamiliar with technical jargon

limitations: Fixed provisional design caps; no universal human capacity bound.
The numeric/source records are authored fixture annotations, not a qualified prose extractor.
Isogloss remains a separately installed advisory text proxy; all rendered requirements have their own required predicates.
Candidate annotations are a declared fixture mapping, not automatic semantic equivalence between rendered text and source.
Each candidate is compared independently with the same baseline; this is a bounded counterexample battery, not a global search or estimated optimum.
